$comment: THE EGRESS TAXONOMY. fleet-manager SPECIFIES this; local-hawk ROUTES on it.
we say which cgroups carry fleet work and must egress direct; local-hawk owns the
nftables/ip-rule policy that puts everything else through the tunnel, and verifies it.
Do NOT add routing, marks, interfaces or CIDRs to this file — that is the other half.
Every entry is a PREFIX match on the observed cgroup path, so a new PM2 service and
a newly-minted JIT runner are covered with no edit here. That is the drift resistance,
and it is why the taxonomy is cgroups rather than a process list.

directEgress.why: ecosystem services and the tunnel that fronts them. A consumer-VPN exit IP in front of the hosted sites is not a posture anyone chose.

directEgress.holds: the standing per-repo runner units, and every JIT runner minted into the same slice
directEgress.why: runners long-poll the GitHub API and move serious volume (356 GB read / 1.6 TB written). A shared consumer-VPN exit is a plausible source of rate limits and flaky long-polls. Treat runners as INFRASTRUCTURE, not as the human.

directEgress.holds: Discord and the Battle.net launcher, placed there by their own launchers
directEgress.why: The third reason for direct egress, and the first that is not about fleet role: these destinations REFUSE a VPN exit. Phase 4 moved unclassified Cloudflare traffic onto the tunnel as designed, and Discord then answered every API call 403 / code 40333 and hung on its "Starting" splash; Battle.net rejected the login as a VPN. Measured 2026-09-13. Nothing malfunctioned -- the taxonomy only encoded "this is fleet infrastructure" as a reason to stay direct, so the operator's own apps fell into "everything else". Membership is a named decision, as hokonLocal is: everything in this slice wears the real WAN address. Add an app only when the service actually blocks the tunnel.

Its WireGuard UDP already escapes the tunnel by fwmark, but its DERP relay connections (TCP 443) did not, so hokon could reach only the Seattle relays — the one /24 allowlisted. On 2026-10-25 an Enshrouded player whose home relay is iad lost their direct path three times between 21:16 and 21:37 PT; each time tailscaled fell back to derp-27 (iad), timed out through nordlynx, and the player was dropped. This settles local-hawk's 2026-09-05 DERP question by identity rather than by maintaining 47 churning relay CIDRs. Everything it sends is WireGuard-encrypted either way; relays see the real WAN address, as Seattle already did.

directEgress.holds: the Enshrouded and Valheim dedicated-server containers, placed there by cgroup_parent in their docker-compose.yml
directEgress.why: Game servers are hokon-local, not fleet work, and egress direct for the same kind of reason as vpnbypass: the tunnel only hurts them. Through nordlynx, Steam registered the server under the NordVPN exit address and every Steam-relay player's traffic took an extra consumer-VPN hop. Named decision 2026-10-25: the real WAN address appears in the Steam server listing.

$comment_ecosystemRoot: A PM2 app is ecosystem when its pm_cwd is this path OR A DIRECTORY UNDER IT.
PREFIX, not equality: mgmt-api runs from srv/hadoku_site/services/mgmt-api, so an
equality test misclassifies the single most important service on the box as unknown.
$comment_hokonLocal: Apps that run under PM2 but are NOT hadoku ecosystem services. They sit in
pm2-hadoku.service, so under the policy above they receive DIRECT egress — that is a
known, accepted leak, not an oversight, and naming them here is what makes it a
decision rather than an accident. An app that is neither under ecosystemRoot nor
listed here FAILS the gate: a new PM2 app silently inheriting fleet egress is the
drift this file exists to catch.
To stop leaking one, the fix is to move it out of PM2 or give it its own slice —
not to delete its line here.

hokonLocal.why: JDownloader clipboard helper — the operator's desktop tooling, no fleet role.
OBS capture sorting under ~/setup/drive-organization — desktop tooling, no fleet role.

Valheim dedicated game server under /mnt/games/valheim-server, with its own ecosystem.config.cjs and wrapper. Nothing in hadoku_site references it and cloudflared has no ingress for it — the operator's game box, no fleet role.
The admin web panel beside it (panel/panel.py, same root). Same classification and the same reason: it fronts the game server only, not anything on hadoku.me.

Enshrouded dedicated game server under /mnt/games/enshrouded-server, same pattern as valheim. The PM2 app is only the docker lifecycle wrapper; the game itself runs in /gameservers.slice (see directEgress). The operator's game box, no fleet role.
PM2's own module, running from ~/.pm2/modules. Not ours and not the operator's; it is the process manager maintaining itself.
